extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students in analysis and PDEs (learning Sobolev spaces and variational methods)
extracted.subtask_description: Properties, structural theorems, and variational formulations for Sobolev spaces W^{m,p} in one dimension, and the associated boundary-value problems (existence, uniqueness, regularity, maximum principle, spectral theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by cut-off and reflection (Lemma 8.3 / Theorem 8.6 argument)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given u ∈ W^{1,p}(I) and a cut-off η, the extension η˜u belongs to W^{1,p}(0,∞) and (η˜u)' = η'˜u + η˜u'. Using such local extensions and reflection one constructs an extension operator P: W^{1,p}(I) → W^{1,p}(R) with controlled norms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct u = ηu + (1−η)u, extend each piece to a half-line by zero and then reflect to obtain v1,v2 ∈ W^{1,p}(R) with controlled L^p and W^{1,p} norms; set Pu = v1+v2. Constants depend on η and its derivatives. This is the standard method to build continuous extension operators from an interval to R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of C_c^∞ approximations (Theorem 8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For u ∈ W^{1,p}(I) (1 ≤ p < ∞) there exists a sequence (u_n) in C_c^∞(R) such that u_n|_I → u in W^{1,p}(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use extension to R, convolution with mollifiers to get smooth approximations and cut-off functions to obtain compact support. Note: in general there may be no approximating sequence from C_c^∞(I) (see remark).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convolution preserves Sobolev regularity (Lemma 8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ρ ∈ L^1(R) and v ∈ W^{1,p}(R) (1 ≤ p ≤ ∞) then ρ* v ∈ W^{1,p}(R) and (ρ* v)' = ρ* v'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove first for ρ compactly supported using duality with C_c^1 test functions; then approximate general ρ by compactly supported ρ_n in L^1 and pass to the limit. This justifies mollification to smooth functions while controlling derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut-off approximation (ζ_n sequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ζ ∈ C_c^∞ with ζ ≡1 on |x|<1 and 0 on |x|≥2, define ζ_n(x)=ζ(x/n). Then ζ_n f → f in L^p(R) for f ∈ L^p(R), 1 ≤ p < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dominated convergence theorem. Combine with mollification to obtain compactly supported smooth approximants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sobolev embedding W^{1,p}(I) ⊂ L^∞(I) (Theorem 8.8, inequality (5))
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists C depending only on |I| such that ||u||_{L^∞(I)} ≤ C ||u||_{W^{1,p}(I)} for all u ∈ W^{1,p}(I) and all 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove first for compactly supported C^1 functions on R via integration and Hölder; then extend by density. Consequence: W^{1,p}(I) continuously injects into L^∞(I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compact embeddings on bounded intervals (Theorem 8.8 parts (6),(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is bounded then (i) W^{1,p}(I) ⊂ C(I) is compact for 1 < p ≤ ∞, and (ii) W^{1,1}(I) ⊂ L^q(I) is compact for all 1 ≤ q < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equicontinuity via the W^{1,p} derivative bound and Ascoli–Arzelà for (i). For (ii) extend functions to R, obtain uniform translation continuity bounds and apply the Kolmogorov–Riesz / Fréchet–Kolmogorov compactness criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Products and integration by parts in W^{1,p} (Corollary 8.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u,v ∈ W^{1,p}(I) with 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ then uv ∈ W^{1,p}(I) and (uv)' = u'v + uv'. Integration by parts formula holds: ∫_y^x u'v = u(x)v(x)−u(y)v(y) − ∫_y^x uv'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use approximation by C_c^1 sequences and pass to the limit. For p=∞, localize to bounded intervals and apply previous case. This demonstrates W^{1,p}(I) is a Banach algebra under pointwise product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain rule / composition in W^{1,p} (Corollary 8.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let G ∈ C^1(R) with G(0)=0 and u ∈ W^{1,p}(I) (1 ≤ p ≤ ∞). Then G∘u ∈ W^{1,p}(I) and (G∘u)' = (G'∘u) u'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When I bounded or p=∞ the restriction G(0)=0 can be relaxed. Prove by approximation u_n → u in W^{1,p} and in L^∞, apply classical chain rule to u_n and pass to the limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and norm of W^{m,p}(I)
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer m ≥ 2, W^{m,p}(I) = {u ∈ W^{m−1,p}(I); u' ∈ W^{m−1,p}(I)}. Equivalently, u has weak derivatives up to order m in L^p. Norm: ||u||_{W^{m,p}} = ||u||_{L^p} + Σ_{α=1}^m ||D^α u||_{L^p}. H^m= W^{m,2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate equivalent norms exist (e.g., using only highest derivative and L^p norm). Many properties for W^{1,p} extend to W^{m,p}, including embeddings into C^{m−1} on bounded intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of W^{1,p}_0 (Theorem 8.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 1 ≤ p < ∞ and u ∈ W^{1,p}(I), u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(I) iff u = 0 on ∂I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One direction: approximating sequence from C_c^1 converges uniformly so boundary values vanish. Conversely, use truncation/composition with a compactly supported function G to build approximants in W^{1,p}_0. This identifies closure of C_c^1(I) in W^{1,p}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations / extensions of W^{1,p}_0 (Remark 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(I) iff the extension by zero u ∈ W^{1,p}(R). (ii) For 1<p<∞, u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(I) iff there exists C with |∫_I u φ'| ≤ C ||φ||_{L^{p'}} for all φ ∈ C_c^1(R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provide useful alternative tests to check membership in W^{1,p}_0 and to identify dual pairings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poincaré inequality on bounded intervals (Proposition 8.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is bounded there exists C depending on |I| such that ||u||_{W^{1,p}(I)} ≤ C ||u'||_{L^p(I)} for all u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(I). Equivalently ||u||_{L^p} is a norm equivalent to the W^{1,p} norm on W^{1,p}_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple proof via integrating from a boundary point and Hölder. This inequality yields coercivity estimates for bilinear forms on W^{1,p}_0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual space representation W^{-1,p'} (Proposition 8.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every F ∈ W^{-1,p'}(I) can be represented by functions f_0,f_1 ∈ L^{p'}(I) such that ⟨F,u⟩ = ∫_I f_0 u + ∫_I f_1 u' for all u ∈ W^{1,p}_0(I), and ||F||_{W^{-1,p'}} = max(||f_0||_{L^{p'}},||f_1||_{L^{p'}}). On bounded I we may take f_0=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via isometry T: u ↦ [u,u'] into L^p×L^p and Hahn–Banach / Riesz representation. f_0,f_1 not unique; one may interpret F as distribution f_0 − (f_1)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak solution definition for boundary-value problems (e.g., (14) and (15))
rubrics_metrics.description: A weak solution of −u'' + u = f on I with Dirichlet boundary condition u=0 on ∂I is u ∈ H^1_0(I) satisfying ∫_I u' v' + ∫_I u v = ∫_I f v for all v ∈ H^1_0(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify appropriate function space and test space, integrate by parts formally and require the identity for all test functions. This is the starting point for variational methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and uniqueness via Lax–Milgram (Proposition 8.15 and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a coercive, continuous bilinear form a(·,·) on a Hilbert space H and linear functional ℓ, there exists a unique u ∈ H with a(u,v)=ℓ(v) for all v∈H. Applied to H=H^1_0(I) and a(u,v)=∫u'v' + ∫uv yields unique weak solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coercivity may follow from Poincaré inequality. Many boundary-value problems are recast into this framework (homogeneous and inhomogeneous Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, Sturm–Liouville after weight transformations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dirichlet's principle / variational characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: The weak solution of −u''+u = f in H^1_0(I) is the unique minimizer of J(v)= (1/2)∫(v'^2+v^2) − ∫ f v over H^1_0(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This minimization formulation is equivalent to Lax–Milgram in the symmetric coercive case and provides variational intuition and numerical discretization bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularity: weak solutions gain derivatives (H^2 regularity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ L^2 and u ∈ H^1_0 is the weak solution of −u'' + u = f, then u ∈ H^2(I); if f ∈ C(¯I) then u ∈ C^2(¯I) (classical solution). More generally, f ∈ H^k ⇒ u ∈ H^{k+2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate the weak relation in distributional sense and use elliptic regularity in 1D: since f−u ∈ L^2, u'' ∈ L^2 so u ∈ H^2. Boundary regularity follows from bootstrapping and embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling inhomogeneous Dirichlet data (Proposition 8.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: To solve −u''+u=f with u(0)=α, u(1)=β, either (1) subtract a smooth function u_0 with the given boundary values and solve for ˜u∈H^1_0, or (2) minimize over the affine closed set K={v∈H^1: v(0)=α,v(1)=β} via Stampacchia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method 1 reduces to homogeneous case. Method 2 uses convex minimization / variational inequalities (Stampacchia's theorem) to obtain existence/uniqueness and then regularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sturm–Liouville and variable-coefficient problems (Example 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For −(p u')' + q u = f on (0,1) with p∈C^1, p≥α>0, q∈C, use H^1_0 and bilinear form a(u,v)=∫ p u' v' + ∫ q u v. If q≥0 then a is coercive and Lax–Milgram gives unique u∈H^1_0 which in fact lies in H^2; classical solution if f∈C(¯I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the bilinear form is not symmetric/coercive due to first-order terms r u', one may multiply by integrating factor ζ=e^{-R} to transform to symmetric weighted form a(u,v)=∫ ζ p u' v' + ∫ ζ q u v and then apply Lax–Milgram when q≥0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neumann, mixed, Robin, periodic, and unbounded-domain formulations (Examples 3–8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each boundary condition corresponds to choosing an appropriate Hilbert space (H^1(I), H^1 with constraints, etc.) and bilinear form; e.g., Neumann uses H^1(I); Robin adds boundary term k u(0) v(0) to the form (coercive if k≥0); periodic uses H^1-periodic subspace; whole-line problems use H^1(R) with vanishing at infinity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt the choice of space and verify continuity/coercivity of the bilinear form (Poincaré not available on whole R). For noncoercive cases, adjust forms or impose conditions (e.g., add zeroth-order term) to regain coercivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum principle for −u''+u = f with Dirichlet data (Theorem 8.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: If u∈H^2(I) solves −u''+u=f on I with u(0)=α,u(1)=β then for every x∈I, min{α,β,ess inf_I f} ≤ u(x) ≤ max{α,β,ess sup_I f}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via Stampacchia truncation: test with G(u−K) for appropriate increasing G vanishing on negative arguments. For classical solutions one can also use pointwise maximum principle arguments (if u attains interior maximum then u''≤0 etc.). Consequences include positivity preservation and L^∞ bounds by boundary and forcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences / corollaries of maximum principle (Corollary 8.20 & Prop 8.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) If u≥0 on ∂I and f≥0 then u≥0 on I. (ii) If u=0 on ∂I and f∈L^∞ then ||u||_{L^∞} ≤ ||f||_{L^∞}. (iii) For Neumann problem with zero mean boundary derivative, inf f ≤ u ≤ sup f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct applications of Theorem 8.19 or its truncation proof. Useful for qualitative behaviour of solutions and a priori bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral decomposition and eigenfunction basis (Theorem 8.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: For p∈C^1(¯I) with p≥α>0 and q∈C(¯I) there exist real eigenvalues λ_n→+∞ and C^2 eigenfunctions e_n forming a Hilbert basis of L^2(I) satisfying −(p e_n')' + q e_n = λ_n e_n with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields orthonormal bases of eigenfunctions for Sturm–Liouville operators and underlies expansions, spectral theory and solution representations. Hypotheses include positive elliptic coefficient p and regularity of coefficients.
